patch_description: The `_reversal_damp` with `keep=0.25` shrinks sub-threshold sign flips but preserves their sign: `out[k] = out[k-1] + keep*d` still yields a difference opposite to `prev_d`, so a downstream reversal counter still registers a flip. This explains why false_reversals has been pinned at 14.2 across four different suppressor stacks. The fix is true flip elimination: on a detected sub-threshold flip, hold the line (out[k] = out[k-1], keep=0) or average the two conflicting steps, applied in a forward sweep plus a mirrored backward sweep for zero phase. The `prev_d` reference must come from the pre-damp difference (not the post-damp zero difference) to avoid zero-stall — with keep=0 the post-step difference becomes 0, which would kill subsequent flip detection if fed back. We retain the corr >= 0.97 guard with a keep=0.5 retry (partial averaging) if pure elimination trips the guard. The zero-difference steps also slightly reduce slope_changes (fewer direction reversals) without touching the genuine large reversals, improving smoothness and false_reversals at essentially zero cost to lag (flips below threshold are noise-scale, not trend-scale).
